source.title: DPN-LE: Dual Personality Neuron Localization and Editing for Large Language Models
source.authors: Lifan Zheng; Xue Yang; Jiawei Chen; Chenyan Wu; Jingyuan Zhang; Fanheng Kong; Xinyi Zeng; Xiang Chen; Yu Tian

record.tranche_reason: The study measures MLP activation patterns under contrasting personality prompts and reports multifunctional as well as trait-exclusive neurons, using a different method from the vision-neuron examples.
record.gate_note: The reported personality activations come from prompts deliberately designed to elicit high- and low-trait responses. The study does not test unrelated tokens or contexts broadly, or quantify what share of neurons have multiple jobs. General-capability results and personality-editing scores are not rows because they do not measure polysemanticity itself.
record.test_reason: This is a personality-editing methods paper. Its 'multifunctional neurons' statement is an interpretation offered to motivate the method. It rests on population-level PCA of MLP activations for high- versus low-trait prompts, plus capability loss under NPTI editing. No neuron's responses to general-knowledge inputs are ever measured. No share of polysemantic neurons is reported, and unrelatedness is never assessed. The reported results are the method's personality-control and capability-preservation scores, so the study relies on the idea rather than testing V2 or any other version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that existing neuron-editing methods modify many neurons unrelated to personality and so degrade capabilities. They assert neurons are multifunctional, linking personality and general knowledge, and that opposing traits show mutually exclusive patterns. They use these trait-exclusive neurons (about 0.5%) for sparse editing. The multifunctionality conclusion is inferred from PCA and capability loss, not measured per neuron.
record.recipe_differences: The study analyzes prompted language-model MLP activations and edits selected neurons during inference; it does not use the original vision-neuron analysis.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported onset of high/low activation separation differs by model: layer 12 for LLaMA-3-8B-Instruct and layer 14 for Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct.

fits_no_version.finding: At the first separating layer, a large fraction of MLP neurons differ between high- and low-trait prompts at |d|>0.8. For Openness this is 40.5% in LLaMA L12 and 50.1% in Qwen L14; trait averages are 28.9% and 39.8% (Table 8). Editing about 20k neurons per trait with NPTI degrades GSM8K by 16-41 points on average (Table 1), which the authors read as overlap between personality and reasoning neurons.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Neurons whose activations distinguish personality-trait prompts in LLM MLPs are widespread. Editing them broadly harms general capabilities, suggesting functional overlap. This is indirect evidence only, not a per-neuron polysemanticity measure.

record.problems: The relevant activation analysis uses deliberately trait-inducing prompts, does not quantify the proportion of multifunctional neurons, and does not establish that personality and general-knowledge responses are unrelated. The Qwen activation-separation result does not itself measure multifunctionality.
record.rows_left_out: Excluded neuron-count thresholds, neuron-selection counts, capability benchmark results, and personality-control scores because they do not directly measure multifunctionality or responses to multiple unrelated inputs.

untested.parts: No neuron-level measurement of responses to unrelated tokens or contexts, and no share of polysemantic neurons by layer. The multifunctionality statement is asserted from PCA and capability loss only.
Initialization, regularization and noise causes not examined.
No architecture, activation-function or regularization comparisons of polysemanticity.
Not examined; Cohen's d threshold choices affect selection counts, but not polysemanticity judgments.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's V2 'supports' and 'limits_scope' labels are removed. The study's evidence cannot show individual neurons responding to unrelated inputs. The 'general knowledge' side is never probed in activation space, and the paper is not a test of polysemanticity prevalence.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not measure unrelated tokens or contexts broadly, quantify the share of polysemantic neurons, or test naturally arising responses without trait-inducing prompts.
Whether polysemanticity is caused by sparse features being packed through superposition.
Polysemanticity arising from initialization, regularization, or training noise without capacity pressure.
Comparisons of activation functions, architecture, or regularization for changing polysemanticity while preserving performance.
Whether canonical mixed-response neurons detect one shared feature or related offshoots of one job.
Whether polysemanticity judgments depend on the activation range examined or on explanation scoring.

rows.subject: LLaMA-3-8B-Instruct
rows.operation_detail: PCA analysis of MLP activations for contrasting high- and low-trait samples; authors report trait-exclusive neurons and multifunctional neurons in intersectional areas.

conditions.value: Big Five high-trait and low-trait prompts

rows.measure: Activation-pattern separation and authors' characterization of neurons in intersectional areas
rows.value: The authors report separable clusters from layer 12 onward; they state that some neurons are trait-exclusive and neurons in intersectional areas relate to both personality traits and general knowledge.
rows.note: This is an explicit multifunctionality finding, but the study does not quantify the size of the intersectional population or establish that the two associated functions are unrelated.
rows.check: PCA shows high/low-trait samples separating from layer 12. It does not measure individual neurons responding to several unrelated inputs. The 'multifunctional' claim is an asserted interpretation with no neuron-level measurement of general-knowledge responses. Prompts deliberately induce traits.

rows.subject: Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct
rows.operation_detail: PCA visualization of MLP activations for contrasting high- and low-trait samples.

conditions.value: Big Five high-trait and low-trait prompts

rows.measure: Separation of activation patterns for opposing personality-trait samples
rows.value: The authors report clearly separable clusters beginning at layer 14.
rows.note: This result does not itself establish that individual neurons respond to multiple unrelated inputs.
rows.check: Only reports onset of high/low-trait cluster separation (layer 14) in Qwen. This is a population representation result, not a polysemanticity measure.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: LLaMA-3-8B-Instruct, high- versus low-trait prompt samples
reader_labels.reason: The authors explicitly report neurons associated with both personality traits and general knowledge in intersectional activation areas; this supports multifunctionality in the tested setting, though not its prevalence. Row R1.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: The analysis also identifies trait-exclusive neurons alongside multifunctional ones, and does not quantify the proportion with multiple functions. Row R1.
